decision.rationale: The framework step-aside established July 24 (reference close $64,177.50, triggering the $65,000 unconditional exit) remains active: today's reference close of $64,657.15 is $342.85 below the re-entry threshold. No reference close above $65,000 has occurred in three consecutive sessions since July 21. Two conditions must be met simultaneously to re-engage: (1) reference close above $65,000 AND (2) net positive Bitcoin ETF flows. Neither is verified: Saturday has no ETF trading, and Friday July 25 ETF flow data was not confirmed as inflow resumption. The two-day recovery ($64,177 → $64,340 → $64,657) is on steadily declining volume (July 24 ~1,206 BTC → July 25 ~580 BTC → July 26 ~312 BTC), limiting its conviction signal. Saturday's $64,944 session high stalled $55 below $65,000 on the day's peak volume (39.79 BTC) — the level held. FOMC July 28-29 is the primary upcoming catalyst: a hawkish hold (with inflation language extending Treasury yield headwinds) extends the step-aside indefinitely; a dovish outcome could rapidly restore risk appetite and ETF inflows, potentially triggering re-entry within 1-2 sessions post-announcement.

analysis:
## Technical analysis

### Session overview — Weekend consolidation, credible base-building pattern
Bitcoin closed the 20:00 UTC reference candle at $64,657.15 on 2026-07-26, up $317.47 (+0.49%) from the July 25 reference close of $64,339.68 (Crypto.com 1h candle, verified). This is the second consecutive positive reference close following the July 24 framework-triggering breakdown to $64,177.50. Session high: $64,944.53 (16:00 UTC 1h candle). Session low: $64,290.57 (06:00 UTC 1h candle). Reference candle volume: 16.74 BTC (~$1.08M at $64,680 average). The framework step-aside protocol from July 24 remains active — the $65,000 reference close re-entry condition has not been met.

### Multi-session reference close progression
| Session | Reference close | Session high | Session low | Change |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| July 21 | $66,402.26 | $66,963.90 | — | Rally peak |
| July 22 | $65,921.39 | $66,742.99 | $65,545.03 | −$480 / −0.72% |
| July 23 | $65,150.56 | $66,317.06 | $64,633.89 | −$771 / −1.17% |
| July 24 | $64,177.50 | $65,812.99 | $63,723.03 | −$973 / −1.49% ← framework exit |
| July 25 | $64,339.68 | $64,449.48 | $63,801.76 | +$162 / +0.25% |
| July 26 | $64,657.15 | $64,944.53 | $64,290.57 | +$317 / +0.49% |

The four-session descending structure (July 21–24) has been followed by a two-session partial recovery (July 25–26). Rising lows: $63,723 (July 24) → $63,801 (July 25) → $64,290 (July 26). This is early base-building. The $65,000 resistance has not been closed above.

### Trend — Bearish structure persists, stabilization beginning
The primary trend remains bearish: BTC has made lower reference closes in four of the past six sessions and has not closed above $65,000 since July 21. However, the two-session recovery with higher session lows is the first evidence that selling pressure is exhausting. The descending triangle from July 21–24 resolved lower (documented in the July 24 analysis); BTC is now consolidating in the post-breakdown range of $63,700–$65,000. A trend reversal requires a reference close above $65,000 — that condition has not been met.

### Momentum — RSI recovering from oversold, returning to neutral
RSI has recovered from the extreme oversold reading of ~28.6 (July 23) to approximately 50 (neutral) per market reports. This oversold-to-neutral recovery is technically expected following a sharp multi-session decline. Critically: neutral RSI at $65,000 provides less inherent bounce energy than oversold RSI at $65,000. If BTC tests $65,000 resistance Monday with RSI at 50 and fails, it is a more technically significant rejection than the July 23 oversold-RSI failure.

### Volume — Weekend illiquidity limits signal value
Saturday session volume was ~312 BTC (00:00–20:00 UTC) — the thinnest session in the recent data series:
- July 26 (Saturday): ~312 BTC session volume
- July 25 (Friday): ~580 BTC session volume
- July 24 (Thursday, breakdown): ~1,206 BTC session volume
- July 22 (Tuesday, active): ~1,400+ BTC session volume

4h candle volume breakdown for July 26:
| 4h Window (UTC) | Volume (BTC) | Range | Note |
|---|---|---|---|
| 00:00–04:00 | 54.6 | $64,349–$64,582 | Asian overnight drift |
| 04:00–08:00 | 41.9 | $64,290–$64,599 | Session low hit at 06:00 |
| 08:00–12:00 | 19.3 | $64,347–$64,580 | Thinnest block — Europe/US gap |
| 12:00–16:00 | 101.7 | $64,410–$64,834 | Strongest 4h — US afternoon push |
| 16:00–20:00 | 77.2 | $64,667–$64,944 | Session high; stalled at $65,000 zone |

The 12:00–16:00 UTC 4h block (101.7 BTC) was the day's strongest volume and drove the push toward $64,944. That push stalled $55 below $65,000 — a micro-scale volume rejection at the framework threshold. Recovery volumes remain well below the July 24 distribution candles (the July 24 12:00–16:00 4h block was 650 BTC, 6× Saturday's equivalent). Low-volume recovery versus high-volume distribution is a weakening momentum signal.

### Pattern — Ascending floor consolidation after triangle breakdown
Post-breakdown pattern: ascending session lows ($63,723 → $63,801 → $64,290) and ascending reference closes ($64,177 → $64,340 → $64,657) within a bounded range topped by the $65,000 resistance. This ascending-floor, flat-ceiling consolidation resolves either upward (if FOMC or ETF flows break $65,000) or downward (if the macro headwinds persist and $63,723 support gives way). Neither side has control on weekend volume.

### Strongest support — $63,723.03 (July 24 session low)
This level has been implicitly tested and held across two subsequent sessions:
- July 24: session low at $63,723 on 150+ BTC volume absorption
- July 25: session low at $63,801 — $78 above $63,723, never retested the exact low
- July 26: session low at $64,290 — $567 above $63,723, continuing to make higher lows

Two sessions of buyers stepping in at progressively higher levels without retesting $63,723 reinforces this as the primary support floor. A reference close below $63,723 activates the triangle measured-move target at approximately $63,000 and signals the base-building pattern was distribution rather than accumulation.

### Strongest resistance — $65,000 (framework threshold / four-test rejection zone)
The $65,000 level has been tested intraday at least four times since July 24 without producing a reference close above it:
- July 24: session high $65,812 → reference close $64,177 (−$822 below $65,000)
- July 25: session high $64,449 → reference close $64,340 (−$660 below $65,000)
- July 26: session high $64,944 → reference close $64,657 (−$343 below $65,000)

Each session the bulls are getting closer to $65,000 at the reference close, but the threshold has not been broken. Saturday's approach to $64,944 on the best volume of the day (39.79 BTC at 16:00 UTC) is the nearest miss. Sellers are defending with conviction even on light weekend volume.

### FOMC as the circuit breaker
The range of $63,700–$65,000 is functioning as a pre-FOMC holding pattern. No participant wants to establish large directional exposure ahead of a binary Fed decision. Once FOMC announces (July 29, ~14:00 ET / 18:00 UTC):
- Hawkish hold: Treasury yields stay elevated → BTC likely breaks $63,723 support → measured-move target $63,000 activated
- Dovish hold or guidance shift: yields compress → risk-on returns → ETF inflows resume → $65,000 reference close becomes achievable within 1-2 sessions → framework re-entry triggered

The framework does not anticipate or position for FOMC outcomes — it responds to the reference close and ETF flow data that result from them.
